newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF floats new product proposals - sources.
newsitem.headline: MATIF floats new product proposals - sources.

text.p: PARIS, Feb 14 (REuter) - French futures and options exchange MATIF submitted to its member firms this week several proposals for new derivatives products, market sources told Reuters on Friday.
The new products being planned include a long yield spread (LYS) contract and a BOBL contract and option which could be launched sometime this year, the sources said.
MATIF distributed documents to dealers that confirmed plans to launch a five-year MATIF contract in 1997 and, in 1998, a "very short term" PIBOR contract.
Reuters obtained a copy of the documents.
A spokesman for MATIF declined to specify the types of products the Exchange was considering but confirmed it was in discussions with members about new offerings.
"We are in consultations with our members. There is nothing sufficiently advanced at this stage for us to announce," MATIF spokesman Jacques Werren told Reuters.

Sources who saw the proposals and participated in meetings with MATIF said the five-year contract would be a notional French government bond with a maturity of four to 5.5 years and a coupon of 4.50 percent.
The deliverable instruments would be French franc BTANs and OATs with residual maturity between four and 5.5 years.
MATIF plans to launch an option on this contract, the sources said.

According to executives at two large French brokerages, MATIF would like to see a BOBL contract and its option traded in Paris, but the written proposal circulated by the MATIF mentions only an option on the BOBL contract that is currently traded on the German DTB exchange.
The plan for the LYS contract is less advanced, the sources said. A U.S. yield curve LYS contract is traded at the Chicago Board of Trade.
MATIF would like to create a spread contract based on different European yield curves, which would be traded on GLOBEX, sources said.

MATIF is also planning to advance the opening of trading in bond futures to 0730 GMT from 0800 GMT, to start at the same time as PIBOR contracts. It wants to keep trading in both PIBOR and Notionnel contracts open until about 1630 GMT. PIBOR contracts now close at 1500 GMT and trading in Notionnel contracts ends at 1530 GMT.
The schedule changes were aimed at taking advantage of trading which now takes place on GLOBEX and matching MATIF hours with those of London's LIFFE, a dealer said.
